text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "In DiffTRe, Uprior is a constant potential encoding a-priori known properties of the system, and it is not a Bayesian prior that biases the learnable parameters in the small data regime [W3168247670#008]. Its first role is to control trajectory generation at the start of the optimization [W3168247670#008][W3168247670#010]. Its second role is to reformulate the problem so that Umodel θ learns the difference between Uprior and the optimal potential, which gives a physics-informed initialization that speeds up convergence [W3168247670#008]. If Uprior contradicts the data, Umodel θ corrects for it during optimization [W3168247670#008]."}
